title: Colors
description: Use colors utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A deliberately paired foreground and surface.
notes: Semantic foregrounds reference --trm-{name}-fg, emphasis and contrast roles. Neutral levels use --trm-fg-body and --trm-fg-1 through -4. The eight semantic names are primary, accent, secondary, success, danger, warning, info and inverse; old text-primary/light/dark aliases are not generated.

sections.heading: Opacity and inheritance
paragraphs: fg-* assigns the non-inheriting --trm-fg composition token. fg-50 mixes that local role with transparent; there is no currentcolor fallback, so pair it with a role. Ordinary CSS color still inherits. fg-reset explicitly inherits the composition token; it is not a hard-coded body color. Lower alpha and weaker role levels can fail text contrast.

sections.heading: Configure foreground roles
paragraphs: Configure the owning theme module before the entry. Theme maps merge shallowly at their top level: replacing one color replaces its whole role map. Use null to remove an exact map key; numeric and quoted string keys are distinct. Test actual pairs in light/dark and forced colors; the pin adds no special CanvasText reminting.

title: Background
description: Use background utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A neutral surface with its body foreground.
notes: Background roles assign --trm-bg and paint background-color. Subtle and muted role families are separate. Neutral body/1–4, foreground, white, black and transparent values come from the theme maps. There are no bg-light/bg-dark or bg-inherit aliases.

sections.heading: Opacity and pairing
paragraphs: bg-50 requires a companion background role because the opacity expression has no fallback for --trm-bg. It changes the background alpha, not child opacity or text color. Choose foregrounds independently; a background class is not a contrast guarantee.

sections.heading: Gradient configuration and mixins
paragraphs: bg-gradient reads --trm-gradient. The enable-gradients switch controls gradient-bg() consumers, not this explicit utility. The pin does not add a forced-colors gradient reset; review decorative backgrounds on supported platforms.

title: Color scheme
description: Use color scheme utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Native color-scheme selection.
notes: These classes set color-scheme to light, dark or light dark. They influence native controls and light-dark() colors, not an application theme toggle. A local scheme does not by itself update the separate root shadow-strength number.

title: Theme
description: Use theme utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A coordinated inverse surface.
notes: theme-{name} supplies inheriting contextual references from --trm-{name}-{role}. Add theme-contrast, theme-subtle, theme-muted or theme-border for paint. These normal-priority utilities are distinct from helper foreground reminting. No theme-color compatibility alias or light/dark color modifier is generated.

sections.heading: Reset and contextual links
paragraphs: theme-reset sets the union of configured context keys to initial, not unset. It removes inherited context rather than repainting a surface. theme-contrast and theme-muted also remint inheriting foreground tokens in the helpers layer; removing a paint utility does not remove that helper rule. Native Reboot links use the contextual foreground when present.

sections.heading: Configure surface utilities
paragraphs: Color modifier names and surface roles do not establish accessibility conformance. The pin primary solid background with white normal-size text can be below 4.5:1; this live example uses inverse. Existing disclosed application contrast customization remains separate from core defaults.

title: Aspect ratio
description: Use aspect ratio utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A native 16:9 box.
notes: ratio-* sets the non-inheriting --trm-ratio token; the upstream [class*=ratio-] selector applies aspect-ratio. This is native sizing, not the old positioned iframe-wrapper helper. Content and min-size constraints can still grow a box; unrelated class names containing ratio- also match the substring selector.

title: Container queries
description: Use container queries utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: This box establishes inline-size containment.
notes: contains-inline and contains-size establish native query containers. They do not generate hidden cq-* display/span rules. Add a real application container query or use the documented container-responsive Grid/stack helpers. A container cannot query itself.

sections.heading: Application query
paragraphs: Give contained layouts a useful available size and test intrinsic sizing. Viewport utility prefixes still query the browser window.

title: Display
description: Use display utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Display includes inline, inline-block, block, grid, inline-grid, table, table-row, table-cell, flex, inline-flex, contents, flow-root and none. Default variants are viewport prefixes only; no infix or print aliases are emitted.

sections.heading: Contents and accessibility
paragraphs: display: contents removes the wrapper box, not its descendants. Test semantics in the supported browser/assistive-technology combinations. display: none removes content from layout and the accessibility tree. Native table elements remain necessary for tabular semantics.

sections.heading: Opt into print display
paragraphs: This replaces the display family and intentionally keeps only block/none. print:d-none is available only after compiling this opt-in map.

title: Float
description: Use float utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: MediaText wraps beside the floated region.
notes: Logical inline-start/end floats support viewport prefixes. Floats do not position flex/grid items. Enclose floats with a formatting context such as flow-root when their parent should contain them.

title: Object fit
description: Use object fit utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
notes: Supply the image box dimensions separately. The scale class maps to scale-down. Fit modes support viewport prefixes. Cropping must not remove essential information; keep useful alternative text.

title: Overflow
description: Use overflow utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example:
Scrollable content remains keyboard reachable.
Check long content at narrow sizes.
Keep focus indicators visible.
notes: Neither the overall nor axis overflow families are responsive by default. Name and keyboard-enable genuinely scrollable regions. Hidden overflow can clip menus, focus outlines or essential content.

title: Position
description: Use position utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Positioned at the start.
notes: Position utilities are not responsive by default. Top/bottom are physical; start/end are logical inline edges. translate-middle uses physical transforms and does not automatically reverse with RTL. Absolute/fixed placement leaves normal flow; preserve layout space and focus visibility.

title: Visibility
description: Use visibility utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Reserved spaceVisible sibling
notes: visible and invisible set visibility. Invisible content retains layout space but is normally absent from the accessibility tree. Old visibility-visible/invisible names are not generated. This is not a data-protection boundary.

title: Z-index
description: Use z-index utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Layer 3 within this stacking context.
notes: Default levels are n1=-1, 0–3, menu=1000, sticky=1010, fixed=1020, drawer=1030, dialog=1040, popover=1050, tooltip=1060 and toast=1070. No dropdown/modal/offcanvas aliases are generated. Ordinary z-index does not escape an ancestor stacking context or outrank the native top layer.

sections.heading: Replace the layer map
paragraphs: This map is replaced, not automatically extended. Keep every key required by the application and its component layer tokens.

title: Align content
description: Use align content utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Distribute wrapped flex lines or Grid tracks along the cross axis; a single flex line is not enough to demonstrate align-content. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Align items
description: Use align items utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Choose cross-axis alignment on a real flex/Grid container with available space. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Align self
description: Use align self utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: StartEnd
notes: Override alignment for one item inside its supporting layout. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Flex
description: Use flex utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Apply d-flex before direction/wrap/grow/shrink controls. Prefixes query the viewport. Reversing visual order does not change reading or keyboard order. flex-fill does not guarantee equal widths when intrinsic content differs.

title: Gap
description: Control both gaps together or space rows and columns independently.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: gap-*, row-gap-*, and column-gap-* use the configured spacer scale: key 2 is .375rem, key 3 is .5rem, and key 4 is .75rem. They work with native Grid and Flexbox and support canonical viewport prefixes such as md:gap-4; infix aliases are not generated. Use row gutters for the percentage-based Flexbox grid; adding a native gap to columns already totaling 100% can cause wrapping.

sections.heading: Independent row and column spacing
paragraphs: gap-3 sets both axes. row-gap-2 and column-gap-4 change the axes independently. In the default scale these are .375rem and .75rem. For a row-oriented flex container, column-gap separates items and row-gap separates wrapped lines. The browser maps Grid rows and columns to the writing mode; the class names do not imply fixed physical x/y axes.

sections.heading: Responsive gaps
paragraphs: md:row-gap-4 applies at the default md minimum viewport width of 768px. Only prefix-style responsive names are generated. Each gap family is responsive by default; print, dark, and state variants require a family override. With equal importance and specificity, the generated cascade order decides the result, not class order in the HTML. Base axis controls follow base gap shorthands, but a wider responsive shorthand can replace both axes; override that axis at the same breakpoint when needed.

sections.heading: Gap configuration
paragraphs: The gap family now uses the same configurable utility map as row-gap and column-gap. Remove a family with null, disable it with enabled: false, or replace its definition. No handwritten gap-* rules are left behind. Definitions are replaced shallowly: supply property, class, values, and any desired flags. The shared spacer map also affects other spacing and gutter helpers. Utilities are not important by default; opt in with important: true on a family, not a global flag.

title: Grid
description: Set Grid track counts, reuse parent tracks, span the full grid, and choose auto-placement.
example:
First
Second
Third
Full explicit row
notes: These mapped utilities configure grid-cols and grid-auto-flow. They do not set display themselves; pair them with d-grid. The grid layout container and g-col/g-start placement API remain independent; strict core has no legacy span aliases. Container-responsive g-col/g-start helpers and automatic grid query containers are available separately through the grid layout API; see the CSS Grid guide.

sections.heading: Track counts and full-width items
paragraphs: grid-cols-1, grid-cols-2, grid-cols-3, grid-cols-4, and grid-cols-6 create equal 1fr tracks, matching the upstream values. There is no default grid-cols-5. Unlike minmax(0, 1fr), a plain 1fr track retains its automatic minimum: long intrinsic content can overflow a narrow box. Use min-w-0, wrapping, and suitable content sizing where needed.

grid-cols-fill belongs on a grid item and sets grid-column: 1 / -1 across all explicit columns. It is not a column count. Use md:grid-cols-3 for the canonical responsive prefix. Grid utilities use shared viewport breakpoints, not container-query variants; infix aliases are not generated.

sections.heading: Subgrid
paragraphs: Place d-grid grid-cols-subgrid on a grid item that spans multiple parent columns to reuse their track lines and column spacing. Add grid-cols-fill to span the entire explicit parent grid. Subgrid is only useful inside a parent Grid; it does not create a standalone set of equal tracks. Check your supported browser versions before depending on it.

sections.heading: Auto-placement and reading order
paragraphs: grid-auto-flow-row places items by row; grid-auto-flow-column places them by column. Set rows and implicit column sizing as appropriate for column flow. grid-auto-flow-dense enables dense row packing, which can visually move later items into earlier holes. CSS placement does not reorder the DOM, reading order, or keyboard tab order. Avoid dense placement for ordered, interactive content when the visual order would become misleading.

sections.heading: Utilities versus layout helpers
paragraphs: Use d-grid for this utility-first API. The grid layout container defaults to twelve 1fr tracks, a 1.5rem gap and inline-size containment. Ordinary children auto-place normally; g-col/g-start set literal placement. Keep track counts and item spans coherent to avoid implicit tracks. See the CSS Grid guide for container-responsive placement.

The new utility families remain available when $enable-cssgrid is false; that switch controls only the layout helper module. Utility removal and configuration use the grid-column-counts, grid-columns, and grid-auto-flow map keys. Declarations are not important by default. Set important: true on an individual mapped family when needed; there is no global importance flag.

sections.heading: Custom track counts
paragraphs: Replacing a definition is shallow. This example intentionally replaces the default track-count family with a five-column value, while keeping fill and auto-flow as separate families.

title: Justify content
description: Use justify content utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: StartEnd
notes: Distribute available main-axis space; behavior depends on the layout direction. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Justify items
description: Use justify items utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Align Grid items or override one item with justify-self. These controls are not a replacement for Flexbox main-axis distribution. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Place items
description: Use place items utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Set combined Grid item alignment using place-items. Use a Grid layout so both axes have meaningful alignment. Viewport prefixes are enabled; generated CSS order decides conflicting classes.

title: Width
description: Use width utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Half the parent width.
notes: Width utilities use physical width, not inline-size, and are not responsive by default. Fixed size-map widths, percentages, auto and intrinsic min/max/fit values are available. Canonical constraints are max-w/min-w, not mw. Viewport units can exceed a padded parent; viewport demos are code-only.

sections.heading: Sizing maps and reserved values
paragraphs: The sizes map contributes to width only, not height. Reserved percentage/auto/min/max/fit width values are merged afterward and win over sizes keys. Configure a whole utility family to replace those values or opt into responsive modes. Physical dimensions do not swap in vertical writing.

sections.heading: Local sizing configuration
paragraphs: These shallow replacements remove fit while changing min to 10rem in each family. They do not claim a shared intrinsic sizing map.

title: Height
description: Use height utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Half the definite parent height.
notes: Height uses physical height and a fixed percentage/auto/intrinsic family, not the numeric sizes map. Percentage heights need a definite containing height. max-h/min-h are canonical; mh aliases and default viewport prefixes are absent. Dynamic viewport units follow changing browser chrome, not just the initial viewport.

sections.heading: Shrinkable content
paragraphs: min-h-0 or min-w-0 can let flex/Grid items shrink below an automatic minimum. Preserve a usable way to read overflowed content rather than clipping essential text.

title: Margin
description: Use margin utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Logical inline-start margin.
notes: Use m/side/x/y prefixes with the shared spacer scale. x/y are logical axes and s/e are inline start/end. Auto margins include responsive prefixes. Negative defaults are only ms--1/me--1 (-.25rem) and ms--2/me--2 (-.5rem), not generic m--*/mx--* or old n spellings.

sections.heading: Spacer defaults
paragraphs: Keys 0–12 are 0, .25, .375, .5, .75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2, 2.25, 2.5 and 3rem. Runtime tokens are --trm-spacer-*. The negative-spacers map is independent of positive spacers.

title: Padding
description: Use padding utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Padding inside the box.
notes: Padding uses the same positive spacer scale as margin. Axes and inline sides are logical; no negative padding is generated. Normal-priority viewport prefixes use md:p-4 rather than infix aliases.

title: Space
description: Use space utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: space-x applies margin-inline-end and space-y margin-block-end to direct children except :last-child. The complete child selector is zero-specificity :where(). This is different from native gap when items wrap or are hidden; match your layout and DOM structure.

title: Font family
description: Use font family utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A monospace identifier.
notes: font-body reads --trm-body-font-family; font-monospace reads --trm-font-mono. These are not responsive by default. Actual glyph coverage and metrics depend on installed fonts; do not use typography alone to communicate meaning.

title: Font size
description: Use font size utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A text-size preset with coordinated line height.
notes: Named fs-* classes set font-size; text-* size presets set font-size and line-height together. Defaults use named tiers, not old numeric fs-1 through fs-6 aliases. Larger tiers can be fluid clamp() expressions. Test zoom, translated labels and available space.

title: Font style
description: Use font style utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: An italic visual treatment.
notes: Use semantic emphasis when text is genuinely emphasized. Font-style utilities are visual controls and are not responsive by default.

title: Font weight
description: Use font weight utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A semibold visual treatment.
notes: Use strong for semantic importance. Available font faces determine whether a weight is native or synthesized. These weight classes are not responsive by default.

title: Line height
description: Use line height utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example:
Comfortable line spacing for this example.
Readability still depends on content and font metrics.
notes: Line-height controls use 1, sm, md and lg. There is no lh-base alias. Tight line heights can clip or overlap enlarged text; test actual content and zoom.

title: Link
description: Use link utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Read the Utility API
notes: Link opacity mixes --trm-link-color in ten-step percentages. Only hover states are generated by default; focus and old hyphen-state aliases are absent. This example explicitly uses the emphasized link-color token for readable text; lower alpha is not a contrast guarantee.

title: Text alignment
description: Use text alignment utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Logical text alignment.
notes: Start/end follow writing direction. Alignment is responsive by default and does not change DOM or reading order.

title: Text decoration
description: Use text decoration utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A visibly underlined destination
notes: Underline offset uses .125/.25/.375em and thickness uses 1–5px. Color assigns the configured foreground-role expression to --trm-underline-color; opacity has a currentcolor fallback. Offset/opacity/thickness have hover states only by default. These controls do not independently change text color.

sections.heading: Customize underline families
paragraphs: The explicit list adds keyboard focus-visible and shallowly replaces the thickness scale. Preserve a usable text/link contrast and do not remove essential link affordances.

title: Text transform
description: Use text transform utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A visual case transformation.
notes: Case transformation does not change the DOM text. Language-specific casing and pronunciation vary; keep accessible names and content understandable.

title: Text wrapping
description: Use text wrapping utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: AnUnbrokenIdentifierThatCanWrapInsteadOfClippingAtNarrowWidths
notes: The pin uses native text-wrap values, not a parallel white-space generator. text-break sets word-wrap and word-break to break-word. text-truncate is a separate single-line helper requiring a constrained block/inline-block box. Browser support varies; CSS.supports can detect pretty wrapping and unsupported engines fall back to ordinary wrapping.

title: Vertical align
description: Use vertical align utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Inline text aligned in the middle.
notes: Vertical-align affects inline-level and table-cell boxes, not flex/Grid alignment. The example uses align-middle with a deliberately larger inline font so the baseline relationship is visible.

title: Border
description: Use border utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A two-pixel border.
notes: Border top/bottom use logical block edges and start/end use logical inline edges; x/y control inline/block axes. Values 1–5 set physical border-width in pixels. border-keyline reads --trm-border-width-keyline. Paint uses the root border width/style/color tokens.

title: Border color
description: Use border color utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Boundary color independent of text color.
notes: Semantic border colors use the theme background role; border-subtle uses the boundary role. Neutral colors reference --trm-border-*. Opacity requires the isolated --trm-bc assignment and has no root-border-color fallback. These classes do not add border width/style by themselves.

title: Border radius
description: Use border radius utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Numeric radius scale.
notes: The numeric 0–9 scale emits literal values into isolated --trm-rounded-size; the base class uses key 5. Circle/pill and logical directional controls are separate. There are no sm/base/lg/xl/xxl aliases. rounded-size changes composition without painting all corners.

sections.heading: Configure the radius scale
paragraphs: Sass changes regenerate literal utility values. Changing a root --trm-radius-* token alone does not rewrite those literals; directional fallbacks and explicit local --trm-rounded-size have separate effects.

title: Divide
description: Use divide utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: FirstSecondThird
notes: Dividers target direct children except :first-child through zero-specificity :where(). x uses border-inline-start and y uses border-block-start. The zero value removes that edge; no new first-child border appears.

title: Pointer events
description: Use pointer events utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Pointer hit-testing is separate from keyboard and semantics.
notes: Pointer-events none does not disable keyboard focus, form submission or script activation. Use native disabled controls and proper semantics for unavailable actions; never use CSS hit-testing as authorization.

title: User select
description: Use user select utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A selectable identifier: project-2026
notes: Selection behavior is not an application security boundary. A text-selectable descendant can override a selection-disabled ancestor where supported. Do not unnecessarily prevent copying important information.

title: Motion
description: Use motion utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: Static preview; motion is not required.
notes: Built-in shake/pop keyframes are decorative. A flat reduced-motion rule disables the stock classes with normal priority. Renamed/custom/state variants need an explicit application preference rule as documented in the Utility API.

sections.heading: Remove mapped animations
paragraphs: The pin checks whether the animation key exists, so null/disabled/renamed definitions still emit global keyframes and flat guards. Only a build that removes the key entirely, such as the filtered Grid entry, omits them. enable-reduced-motion: false removes the guard, not the keyframes.

title: Opacity
description: Use opacity utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A fully opaque readable preview.
notes: Opacity affects the entire element and its descendants, including text and focus indicators. The default family has no responsive/state/print/dark variants. Zero opacity can leave invisible interactive controls; use suitable hiding or disabled semantics instead.

title: Shadows
description: Use shadows utilities from the configured Tremplin utility map.
example: A composable decorative shadow.
notes: Shadow utilities emit literal oklch relative-color expressions rather than reading an old shadow runtime alias. Isolated --trm-sc selects color and --trm-so controls strength: opacity-50 means multiplier 1 and opacity-100 means 2. Global --trm-shadow-color remains an inheriting fallback; theme dark strength is 2.4 versus light 1.

sections.heading: Customize a composable shadow
paragraphs: The shadows map is replaced and uses null for the suffixless class, not base. The enable-shadows mixin switch does not remove these literal utilities. Native forced-color adjustment and relative-color support need platform testing; the pin adds no blanket forced-color reset.
